title: DocMonk Relationship-Building Performance Optimization

branch_strategy.model: small feature branches based on the latest main, one PR per phase
rules: Rebase each phase onto main after its prerequisites are merged.
Keep performance-only PRs separate from semantic changes where possible.
Require baseline and post-change benchmark comparisons in each PR.
Do not perform a clean-slate reset or force a repository-wide reindex as part of the rollout.

observed_workload.note: File and entity counts are user-reported; relationship count, graph duration, and per-phase timings must be measured before attributing the slowdown.

verified_code_findings.description: Phase 1 extracts entities, while the relationship stage reads, SHA-hashes and parses files again to derive edges.
The server graph staging function loads the file list and issues file_relationships() separately for each file; this creates an N+1 SQLite access pattern on large sources.
Code-document linking loads all entities, all link units and routes, then constructs a fresh UnitIndex for each nonempty linking pass.
Full cross-file resolution materializes all code entities and cross-file references; selective resolution already exists and must be preserved.
Server copy-forward uses synchronous update-by-query per batch and generation, followed by refresh and fenced promotion.

already_implemented_do_not_duplicate: Two-stage indexing/relationships barrier and separately published graph generations
skip and rebind plans for current or semantically identical graphs
incremental changed-file graph derivation and per-file symbol dependencies
selective cross-file resolution based on changed symbol definitions
parallel file derivation in batches of 256
server-side unchanged-graph copy-forward and fenced atomic publication

objectives: Reduce time to a complete, searchable relationship graph for large code sources.
Make incremental graph updates proportional to changed files and affected symbol dependents rather than total corpus size.
Reduce unnecessary database queries, allocations, and OpenSearch/Elasticsearch update operations.
Maintain exact graph semantics, deterministic relationship IDs, stable evidence, and safe atomic visibility.
Show users precisely where a long-running relationship pass spends its time.
non_goals: Changing the public meaning of callers, callees, references, impact, or document-code links.
Removing writer leases, publication barriers, generation fencing, or crash safety.
Dropping support for local SQLite, OpenSearch, or Elasticsearch.
Requiring users to delete indexes or run a complete file reindex to activate the improvements.
Blindly raising thread counts or bulk sizes without workload measurements.
Disabling correctness checks to make performance numbers look better.

correctness: Cold and incremental graph outputs match a deterministic canonical baseline for relationships, document links, confidence, resolver, evidence, and target IDs.
An unchanged source plans 'skip'; a semantically equivalent republished base plans 'rebind' when eligible.
A body-only edit does not re-resolve unrelated references, while added/removed/renamed/ambiguous symbols update every affected dependent.
A graph built from files that changed after indexing is never published as if it matched the base snapshot.
Failed, cancelled, superseded, or lease-lost builds never expose an incomplete graph.
All public retrieval and MCP graph outputs are equivalent to the pre-optimization behavior.

performance_goals_not_benchmarked_claims.cold_full_graph_target: Aim for at least 2x faster graph-stage wall-clock on the representative 8,205-file source; record actual result, and do not ship a slower end-to-end indexing plus relationship pipeline.
performance_goals_not_benchmarked_claims.incremental_edit_target: Aim for at least 5x faster than baseline on a one-file edit if baseline does material work; skip/rebind should perform no graph publication.
performance_goals_not_benchmarked_claims.server_staging_query_target: Replace approximately one file_relationships() query per source file with one streaming query or bounded paginated reads; count and report actual queries.
performance_goals_not_benchmarked_claims.quality_regression_budget: Zero graph-output differences for deterministic fixtures and validated sampled production cases.
performance_goals_not_benchmarked_claims.resource_regression_budget: No uncontrolled memory growth; record peak RSS, CPU time, SQLite query counts, network traffic and cluster workload.

success_criteria.decision_rule: Targets are engineering hypotheses, not existing measurements. Accept each optimization only when correctness passes and repeatable benchmark results justify its complexity.

execution_principles: Instrument first; optimize the measured critical path.
Track whole-run indexing+graph wall time as well as graph-only time, since caching extraction may shift work to indexing.
Prefer local, exact, indexed lookups and bounded streaming over loading entire tables repeatedly.
Maintain content-hash and derivation-version provenance for any reusable reference facts or linking indexes.
Be deterministic: stable ordering, IDs, tie-breaking, ambiguous resolution and output hashes.
Treat OpenSearch/Elasticsearch as authoritative for visible server generations, with local staging only as a verified cache.
Keep config defaults behavior-compatible; use experimental feature flags for changes that affect persistence or graph publication.
Support incremental adoption and safe cache regeneration without destructive reindexing.

phases.name: Profiling, baseline and reproducible benchmark harness
phases.purpose: Identify whether derivation, linking, SQLite staging or server publish dominates this workload before tuning.

tasks.title: Add phase-level timers
tasks.details: Measure planning, cache access, file reads/hash, parsing+edge derivation, SQLite edge writes, symbol manifest load/build, cross-file resolution, document link generation, graph staging, copy-forward, server bulk write, refresh, and promotion. Use monotonic timers.

tasks.title: Add counters and structured diagnostics
tasks.details: Track files scanned/derived/reused, references examined and updated, candidates looked up, links evaluated/written, per-file SQL queries, server HTTP requests/bytes, files copied/written, edges and links staged, and retries. Retain existing JSON fields and add optional fields.

tasks.title: Expose stage-specific progress
tasks.details: Show phases such as deriving, resolving, linking, staging, copying and promoting; do not misleadingly report 100% when only file derivation completed. Add heartbeat during long phases.

tasks.title: Build benchmarks
tasks.details: Implement synthetic reproducible fixtures near 8,205 files and 57,442 entities, plus optional privately run real-workload benchmarks. Cover cold, no-change, one body edit, one definition rename, file add/remove, doc edit, cross-source dependency, and staging-cache recovery.

tasks.title: Collect baseline
tasks.details: Run repeated warmups and at least 5 measured runs per scenario on SQLite and the actual server backend. Report median/p95 wall time, CPU, peak RSS, SQL queries, server traffic and relationship/link counts. Record storage hardware, workers, batch sizes, and version SHA.

tests: JSON backwards-compatibility and stable reason/action fields
No secret path or document content logged
acceptance_criteria: Baseline results are stored as machine-readable JSON with a readable comparison report.
All material phases are timed independently; sum of phases plausibly accounts for total duration.
The 8,205-file/57,442-entity class of workload can be run repeatedly without publishing proprietary source code.
No graph-semantic change occurs in this phase.

phases.name: Eliminate per-file graph staging queries
phases.purpose: Remove the N+1 SQLite read pattern in graph staging and reduce allocations without changing graph publication semantics.

tasks.title: Create ordered relationship row streaming API
tasks.details: Add a build-scoped, ordered cursor/iterator (ORDER BY file_id, id) or bounded page API in ProjectStore; prefer prepared SQLite statements and projection of only required columns.

tasks.title: Group staged edges in one pass
tasks.details: Replace stage()'s store.file_relationships(build, file_id) loop with a single ordered traversal. Group edges by file_id and preserve exact deterministic digest ordering and link grouping.

tasks.title: Bound memory
tasks.details: Avoid constructing redundant full copies of graphs when streaming and computing per-file digests; preserve enough canonical manifest information to identify changed files. Measure peak memory before/after.

tasks.title: Use bounded server writer and equivalent digests
tasks.details: Feed staged file groups into the existing bulk writer, preserving unchanged file digest comparisons, conflict checks, and generation promotion. Avoid altering edge IDs and canonical JSON hashing unexpectedly.

tasks.title: Benchmark
tasks.details: Count SQLite statements and compare staging_seconds, allocations, RSS and total publish time on small and 8,205-file sources.

tests: Relationships with multiple edges per file
No missing or duplicated edges on pagination boundaries
acceptance_criteria: No per-file SQLite relationship lookup on the full-graph server staging path.
Canonical staging digest and published graph rows match the baseline.
Staging runtime and/or query count materially improves without increasing peak RSS uncontrollably.

phases.name: Reuse parsed reference facts from indexing
phases.purpose: Avoid parsing the same source a second time just to derive structural/reference graph facts; keep visible graph publication as phase 2.

tasks.title: Define stable reference-fact artifact
tasks.details: Define a compact per-file representation of extracted structural edges, calls, imports, inheritance, decorators, framework edges, and unresolved reference text. Key it by file ID, content SHA-256, code extraction version and graph-fact format version. Preserve line locations and deterministic IDs.

tasks.title: Capture facts from the existing parse
tasks.details: During CodeProcessor::prepare, derive reusable reference facts from the same tree-sitter parse as entity extraction. Keep graph resolution and public graph visibility out of stage 1. Measure added indexing time and artifact size.

tasks.title: Add bounded local persistence and lifecycle
tasks.details: Persist facts with the file's indexing transaction or a safely committed content-addressed cache. Copy forward unchanged facts, invalidate changed/version-incompatible facts, and garbage-collect unreferenced artifacts. Avoid duplicate large JSON blobs in metadata.

tasks.title: Consume reusable facts during relationship build
tasks.details: In derive_batch(), load facts when provenance matches the exact published file and derivation; otherwise fall back to the existing read-hash-parse path. Do not reindex existing sources merely to fill missing caches.

tasks.title: Preserve snapshot integrity
tasks.details: Do not weaken stale-source detection. Either rehash current bytes against the published hash when using cached facts or consume a verified immutable source snapshot; if changed, mark stale rather than publishing a mismatched graph.

tasks.title: Feature-gated rollout
tasks.details: Add an internal/configurable cache flag with a safe default and fallback, metrics for cache hit/miss/fallback, and clean cache invalidation when derivation changes.

tests: Cold cache, warm cache and partially missing cache
Stable IDs and ordinals for overloaded C# symbols
acceptance_criteria: A cache hit does not invoke the tree-sitter parse a second time during graph derivation.
Cached and uncached relationship graphs are identical for all golden fixtures.
An old existing index remains usable and graphs build via fallback when facts are absent.
End-to-end index plus relationship time is measured; optimization is not accepted solely because work shifted into indexing.

phases.name: Persistent incremental code-document linker
phases.purpose: Make document linking scale with changed code symbols, changed document chunks, and their reverse dependents, not the entire source.

tasks.title: Measure linker fan-out
tasks.details: Record entity rows loaded, document units loaded, UnitIndex construction time, matching time by resolver, emitted link count, and manual projection time.

tasks.title: Build versioned reverse lookup indexes
tasks.details: Store a reusable build-scoped inverted map from normalized identifier tokens to document unit IDs and from document unit IDs to candidate symbol keys, with Unicode boundary semantics identical to matcher.rs. Use bounded per-source shards rather than one giant metadata JSON value.

tasks.title: Compute change impact
tasks.details: On modified code, re-evaluate changed definitions and relevant units; on modified documents, re-evaluate changed units against relevant entities. Preserve filename, alias, qualified-name and route matching, not just exact symbols.

tasks.title: Handle removed/renamed/ambiguously matched inputs
tasks.details: Delete obsolete automatic links that depend on removed entities/units, rebuild all affected dependent link candidates, and preserve manual links independently of automatic link caches.

tasks.title: Avoid rebuilding global indexes each pass
tasks.details: Load reusable indexes or partial shards, update only changed postings, and cap memory during candidate generation. Maintain a conservative full fallback if index or manifest cannot be validated.

tasks.title: Regression and performance comparisons
tasks.details: Compare outputs of old full linker, new full linker and incremental linker over code-only, docs-only, mixed and large-corpus fixtures; include common identifiers to reveal candidate explosion.

tests: Unicode word boundaries and dotted identifiers
acceptance_criteria: A one-file code edit does not reload and rebuild every unrelated document matching unit.
A changed document chunk updates links for unchanged but affected code entities.
No missing, stale or duplicate links relative to full graph recomputation.
Fallback can rebuild a corrupt or absent linker cache safely without reindexing documents.

phases.name: Batch and cache symbol candidate resolution
phases.purpose: Reduce repeated symbol lookups on incremental builds and memory overhead on full builds while preserving deterministic ambiguity rules.

tasks.title: Instrument resolution cost
tasks.details: Count distinct qualified/bare names, cached lookups, candidate rows, reference rows, affected files, SQL calls and changed outcomes for both resolve_build() and resolve_files().

tasks.title: Batch candidate queries
tasks.details: For selective resolution, gather distinct reference keys from affected files and retrieve candidates in bounded batches rather than issuing a separate statement per new name; reuse existing SQLite name and qualified-name indexes.

tasks.title: Make reverse dependencies explicit
tasks.details: Use the existing FileSymbols manifest as source of truth and optionally materialize a bounded reverse postings index keyed by q: and n: symbol keys. Do not mark every file dirty for a body-only edit.

tasks.title: Optimize full resolution
tasks.details: Build compact deterministic candidate tables once, process references in bounded ordered chunks, and batch only changed resolution updates. Compare memory versus the existing all_entities() approach.

tasks.title: Validate cross-source behavior
tasks.details: Preserve explicit project reference and declared dependency scoping, candidate-fingerprint invalidation, ambiguous producer handling, and retry after unavailable dependencies.

tests: Definition added, removed, moved or renamed
Multiple qualified-name candidates and stable tie-breaking
Changed downstream consumer without producer change
acceptance_criteria: Selective resolution touches only affected files and relevant candidate symbols.
Resolution outputs match old resolve_build() for all test cases and random generated fixtures.
No unbounded per-name query explosion on a source with many references.

phases.name: Optimize OpenSearch and Elasticsearch graph generations
phases.purpose: Reduce server-side generation copy and bulk overhead, not just local graph derivation time.

tasks.title: Profile copy-forward and publish separately
tasks.details: Count _update_by_query calls, updated docs, bulk records, copied files, bytes, refresh duration, cluster throttling/retries and promotion latency. Compare OpenSearch with Elasticsearch on identical fixtures.

tasks.title: Avoid avoidable server writes
tasks.details: Honor skip/rebind and per-file digests first; use no mutation when graph is current or has semantically identical inputs. Verify skipped publication after staged cache recovery.

tasks.title: Tune bounded copy-forward
tasks.details: Bench test configurable COPY_BATCH, bounded concurrency and the existing bulk settings. Only use asynchronous _update_by_query after adding task polling, cancellation and complete failure verification; never promote until all tasks finish.

tasks.title: Investigate immutable graph-fragment reuse
tasks.details: If copy-forward remains dominant, design an optional manifest referencing immutable per-file graph fragments across generations. Prototype separately with read-path changes, safe garbage collection, pinning and lease fencing. Do not implement or enable unless the measured result justifies the added complexity.

tasks.title: Keep bounded generations and safe cleanup
tasks.details: Enforce atomic pointer promotion, retained old-reader generations, retries, stale build handling, orphan cleanup and idempotent failed publishes.

tests: Lease lost while copy is running
acceptance_criteria: Every published graph remains visible only after all referenced records are complete.
Server-mode graph publication produces fewer requests or less elapsed time for large-source incremental updates.
The old graph remains queryable after failure, conflict or interrupted copy-forward.

phases.name: Worker scheduling and bounded memory
phases.purpose: Use CPU, disk and server capacity effectively without fighting SQLite writer limitations or starving other repositories.

tasks.title: Benchmark GRAPH_BATCH and parser workers
tasks.details: Compare 64/128/256/512 files per batch and workers 1/2/4/8 or CPU-limited values; record parse throughput, RSS and time in SQLite writes. Avoid a global default based on one machine.

tasks.title: Limit concurrent sources and work queues
tasks.details: Use global CPU/IO/semaphore budgets and bounded producer-consumer queues, while preserving one writer per source and lease ownership. Verify fairness across many sources.

tasks.title: Preserve two-stage barrier
tasks.details: Index each selected source and publish all bases before cross-source dependency resolution, or explicitly prove a source-local optimization cannot observe unfinished producers.

tasks.title: Make progress responsive
tasks.details: Heartbeat during long SQL reads, linking loops and server copy tasks so active passes are not mistaken for dead leases.

acceptance_criteria: No unbounded queue or memory growth during graph construction.
Concurrent multi-source runs remain fair and do not corrupt or publish mixed snapshots.
Chosen defaults are supported by benchmark results rather than guessed thread counts.

phases.name: Correctness gates, end-to-end validation and rollout
phases.purpose: Prove speed improvements without semantic regression, and introduce cache or publication changes safely.

tasks.title: Graph equivalence validator
tasks.details: Build an automated comparator that normalizes and hashes all edges, links, resolvers, confidence, source location, evidence and graph query outputs for baseline versus optimized runs.

tasks.title: Create workload matrix
tasks.details: Benchmark cold, warm, incremental, code-only, mixed docs+code, dependency chain, staging cache loss, interrupted writes and 150-repository load using both SQLite and server storage.

tasks.title: CI smoke performance guards
tasks.details: Run fast deterministic correctness/perf smoke checks per PR. Run time-consuming large workload benchmarks manually or in nightly jobs; fail CI only on stable thresholds to avoid timing noise.

tasks.title: Rollout flags and fallbacks
tasks.details: Ship optional new fact-cache/linker-index paths with metrics and ability to fall back to old algorithms. Use lazy regeneration for stale artifacts; no mandatory destructive reindex.

tasks.title: Document operations
tasks.details: Explain graph phase reporting, skip/rebind/full/retry, caching, cache invalidation, storage footprint and backend parity. Add troubleshooting for long 'building' or 'publishing' statuses.

tasks.title: Benchmark report and final review
tasks.details: Attach before/after tables with stage timings, whole-run timings, throughput, p95, memory, query/HTTP counts and output-equivalence results. Label measured vs target clearly.

tests: Golden fixtures and randomized change sequences
Real-backend OpenSearch and Elasticsearch tests where environments are available
acceptance_criteria: All required correctness gates pass on local and server backends.
Benchmark artifact includes measured results for a workload comparable to 8,205 files and 57,442 entities.
No mandatory reindex and a tested rollback path for new caches and graph generation changes.
The final report identifies the largest measured improvement and remaining bottleneck.

benchmark_matrix.mutation: Base index published; no usable graph/cache yet
benchmark_matrix.expectation: Full graph equivalent to baseline; report derivation/linking/publish separately

benchmark_matrix.mutation: Run relationships build again without any new publication
benchmark_matrix.expectation: Skip; zero edges rewritten and zero graph publication

benchmark_matrix.mutation: New base generation, identical semantic file keys
benchmark_matrix.expectation: Rebind if eligible; no expensive graph rebuild

benchmark_matrix.mutation: Edit an implementation without changing symbol definitions
benchmark_matrix.expectation: Only necessary file facts; avoid unrelated re-resolution

benchmark_matrix.mutation: Change a symbol referenced by other files
benchmark_matrix.expectation: Re-resolve changed file and referencing dependents; no stale targets
Match full resolver output and tie-breaking

benchmark_matrix.mutation: Change a chunk mentioning a code entity
benchmark_matrix.expectation: Update link edges even if code files are unchanged
Delete invalid edges and relink affected dependents

benchmark_matrix.mutation: Remove only local server staging cache; keep server graph
benchmark_matrix.expectation: Safe server rehydration/fallback without silent semantic drift

benchmark_matrix.mutation: Change source after indexing or interrupt server publication
benchmark_matrix.expectation: Stale/failed result, no partial graph exposed

benchmark_matrix.mutation: 150 sources with mixed sizes and explicit dependencies
benchmark_matrix.expectation: Bounded resource use, fair scheduling, correct cross-source graph

reporting_rules: Emit optional additional keys, do not rename/remove existing JSON fields.
Do not expose file contents, source paths, tokens or credentials in metrics.
Separate index-stage and relationship-stage time; compute end-to-end time as well.
Represent no-op skips explicitly rather than assigning a misleading zero-duration full build.

technical_invariants: Graph relationships are not visible until the exact base generation is validated and graph generation is atomically promoted.
Keep the existing writer lease, fencing checks and publication CAS semantics.
Cross-file candidates and ambiguity are deterministic and scoped exactly as before.
Only changed resolution outcomes cause row updates; unchanged edges retain stable IDs.
Schema additions and caches cannot force destructive resets or invalidate already published searchable content.
Any optimization cache is disposable: incorrect, absent or old artifacts cause safe recomputation.
Doc-to-code linking includes unchanged code affected by document changes and unchanged docs affected by code changes.
Manual link intent is preserved across automatic relinking and failed publishes.
Server graph copy-forward keeps old-reader generation pins valid until readers release them or retention policy expires.
Optional optimizations must preserve mixed Windows/Linux path handling and current C# parsing behavior.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Persisting reference facts moves cost from graph stage into indexing
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Benchmark whole-run time, keep facts compact, use fallback, and only enable by default after a verified net win.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Incorrect reverse index misses links or dependent references
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Canonical baseline comparisons, property-based change-sequence tests, derivation version checks, conservative full rebuild fallback.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Caching stale facts after a file changes during indexing
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Key by published content SHA-256 and verify current source hash or immutable snapshot before graph promotion.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Over-optimistic OpenSearch async copy publishes incomplete generations
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Fence tasks by lease and expected base, await verified completion and failures, then promote with CAS.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Large caches or inverted indexes consume excessive RAM/disk
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Bounded shards/pages, TTL/garbage collection, RSS and artifact-size budgets, lazy regeneration.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Concurrency tuning contends on SQLite single-writer or OpenSearch backpressure
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Single writer per source, bounded queues, quotas, retry/backoff and measured resource limits.
Multi-source benchmarks, global concurrency governor and fairness checks.

quick_win_note: P1 is the smallest high-confidence performance change and can be implemented immediately after instrumentation. P2 and P3 are the most promising but higher-risk architectural changes. Prioritize the actual measured slowest phase after P0.
claude_code_execution_prompt: Implement DocMonk Relationship-Building Performance Optimization in https://github.com/gzarog/DocMonk. Read this JSON plan and inspect the current main branch before changing code. Work in the specified phase order with one feature branch and PR per phase against main. P0 must establish repeatable baseline profiling first. Preserve all existing skip/rebind/incremental semantics, deterministic graph IDs and evidence, cross-source dependencies, writer leases and atomic graph publication. Do not delete indexes or force a full reindex. Implement P1's bulk graph staging, P2's safe versioned reference-fact reuse, P3's correct incremental document linker, P4's candidate lookup improvements, P5's measured server publication optimizations, and P6's resource controls. Where code differs from the reviewed tree, adapt the design rather than blindly applying instructions. Run Rust formatting, clippy, workspace tests, graph golden/regression tests, and realistic before/after benchmarks. For every PR report changed files, actual measured performance, peak memory, graph equivalence, tradeoffs, and rollback behavior. Do not claim a speedup until verified. Complete P7 with an implementation and benchmark report.
